4.2.3 Isolation Forest — Anomaly Detection 
Isolation Forest (Liu, Ting, and Zhou, 2008) was selected as the unsupervised 
anomaly detection algorithm. This method functions by randomly selecting a feature 
and a split value to recursively partition the data. Anomalous points are isolated with 
fewer splits, resulting in shorter mean path lengths and lower anomaly scores. The 
algorithm was selected due to three main advantages: it is tree -based and scale -
invariant, eliminating the need for feature normalization; it has O(n log n) processing 
complexity and completed training within seconds on 82,069 reviews; and it provides 
interpretable anomaly scores and feature significance rankings.  The model was 
configured with n_estimators=200, increased from the default of 100 to increase 
stability, contamination=0.10, and random_state=42.  Twenty-one numeric features 
from Phase 1 serve d as input.  The model identified 8,207 anomalies, representing 
10.00% of all reviews.

The aim of this project was to develop an analytical system for improving insight quality 
in Amazon app reviews by combining sentiment analysis with fake review/anomaly 
detection. 
 
Objectives: 
1. To collect and preprocess a dataset from Amazon user reviews and conduct 
exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover patterns.  
2. To develop an unsupervised anomaly detection system to detect unusual review 
behaviour. 
3. To implement a sentiment analysis model to classify positive, neutral, and negative 
sentiments. 
4. To design an interactive dashboard that supports real -time analysis by allowing 
users to input custom text and receive instant sentiment classification and review 
detection.
